prerequisites: The student has already followed first semester courses in phase 1.

learning_outcomes.text: The student is able to formulate a clear problem statement, objective, and assignment for electronic or ICT systems in consultation with stakeholders.
The student substantiates the assignment through analysis and research.
The student is able to develop an electronic or ICT system for a proof of concept or service that meets a number of conditions.
The student is able to realize a relevant implementation within the set conditions.
The student justifies the choices made for the different components.
The student delivers a working proof of concept solution or service.
The solution is a complete and correct implementation of established requirements.
The student verifies and validates the product or service against the stated requirements.
The student documents the realization process.
The student makes technological systems function in their application context or working environment.
The student compiles a documentation bundle with a view to reproducing and maintaining it.
The student communicates purposefully about the assignment using the main current communication forms and techniques.
The student is able to clearly summarize the various aspects of their project, articulate them verbally and in writing, and present them visually.
The student can offer relevant advice to third parties in relation to his/her design and the associated process.
This applies to a wide variety of stakeholders and potential target groups.
The student has insight into their own entrepreneurial ability.

The student demonstrates an entrepreneurial attitude including a sense of initiative, out-of-the-box thinking, perseverance, design thinking, critical thinking, self-knowledge, and action orientation.
The student takes into account the commercial feasibility of their project.
The student strives for quality work in project and performance management.
The student carries out their own tasks as independently as possible and works in a solution-oriented manner.
The student directs, evaluates, and optimizes their own effectiveness.
The student adjusts based on feedback.
The student approaches assignments in a project-based manner and respects planning and budgetary context, making adjustments if necessary.
The student functions in a team-oriented and entrepreneurial manner.
The student adopts a constructive attitude as an expert member of a (project) team with a view to their own (future) role and responsibility within a company or organization.
The student thinks in an international and digital working environment.

syllabus_topics: Project development based on student's own chosen topic
Self-reliant project work in lab sessions
Approval of project proposal by supervising lecturer
Presentation and defense of project results
assessment_rules: The overall grade is on a scale of 1-20. The Practice Enterprise (lab) component accounts for 100% of the grade. The Practice Enterprise (theory) component has a 0% weighting, as the taught material is implicitly assessed through the presentation/realization of the project, meaning the score for the lab is also the score for the theory. Partial transfers are possible for successful partial results within the academic year. No new project can be submitted for the resit.
